title: 2.1 · Bug hunt (Test and debug)
name: Bug hunt (Test and debug)
summary: Students fix programs that are already written and already broken. In the Debug Lab every level starts with a broken program: a wrong turn, a loop count one too many, a missing block, a wrong condition, a block out of order, an extra block inside a loop, and two bugs at once on the last level. Pairs step through it one block at a time, say what they expected and what Bolt did, change only that block, and test again. Fewest edits earn the most stars.
iCan: find and fix a mistake in a program, mine or someone else's
say what I expected and what actually happened
test a program before I say it is done
materials: Bug Cards printable (printed programs with one bug each, grid mats, fix stickers)
doNow: Find the mistake in each one: 2 + 2 = 5. Teh cat sat on the mat. A route card that says turn left when the flag is on the right.
plan: Explore: a broken program in step mode, the class says Stop!

warmup.why: first lesson of the unit: the unit opener, the vocabulary item and today's three exit items as a pre-test; nobody is expected to know them yet, so say so

do: Open Robo Route at Debug Lab on the projector (Open game at this chapter). Level 1 already has a program: forward, forward, forward, turn left, forward, forward, forward. Press Run once and let it fail: Bolt turns away from the flag and bumps.

Press Step instead. One block at a time, the class watches and says Stop! the moment Bolt does something they did not expect. It is the turn left. Change only that block to turn right and run again. Point at the edits counter: one edit, three stars.
say: Programs break. Good programmers expect it and test. A mistake in a program is called a bug; finding and fixing it is debugging.
The best first move is not deleting everything. It is stepping through and asking two questions: what did we expect, and what actually happened? The bug lives where those two first split apart.
ask: What did we expect? What actually happened?
explore.afterAsk: Write expected and actual on the board as two columns. Fill them in for level 1: expected a turn toward the flag; actual a turn away. Leave the columns up for Play.
explore.bigIdea: To fix a bug, step through the program, find where expected and actual first split apart, change that one thing, and test again.

play.stretch: the chapter, then 3 stars: the fewest edits on every level
play.pairs: driver and navigator on one device; the Swap! banner shows every 3 levels; the navigator reads the starter program out loud before the first run and says Stop! in step mode
lookFors: pairs deleting the whole program instead of stepping through it
fixing by adding blocks around the bug instead of changing the wrong block: the edits counter goes up and the stars go down
saying done after the change without running the program again
play.misconception: A fix is not done when the program looks right: it is done when you run it again and Bolt does what you expected.
earlyFinishers: help a neighbor without touching their screen

discuss: What was the bug on level 5, and how did you find it? Show step mode.
Why is deleting everything a slow way to fix a bug?
showMe: One pair steps through level 5 on the projector; the class says Stop! at the first block that does something unexpected.

exit.sentencePrompt: Pick one bug you fixed today. What did you expect, what did Bolt actually do, and what did you change?
exit.frame: I expected ___ but Bolt ___, so I ___.

rubric.line: Debugging: expected, actual, and the fix
levels: Says something went wrong or names a bug with no detail
Says what was expected, what Bolt actually did, and the change that was made
Also says how the bug was found: step mode, the first wrong block, or testing again after the fix

exit.paper: exit half-sheet (two per page) with the three items and the sentence frame

support: hint 1 highlights the block where expected and actual first differ
the navigator reads the starter program out loud before the first run; read-aloud on
levels 1 to 6 have exactly one bug each; only level 7 has two
stretch: 3 stars on every level: the fewest edits
level 7 has two bugs: fix one, test, then find the other
Best Route, the next chapter: open the game from Games rather than from this lesson and enter quest code 7 1 0 0; two programs both work, pick the better one and improve it

unpluggedTwin.title: Bug Cards
materials: printed programs with one bug each
one grid mat per pair with a start and a flag
steps: Each pair gets a bug card: a short program and the grid it should solve. One partner is the computer and moves the token one card line at a time; the other says Stop! at the first line where the token does something unexpected.
Write the two columns on the back: expected and actual. Then fix only that one line with a sticker. Run the whole program again from the top to prove it.
Swap bug cards with another pair. Try to fix the new card with one sticker. Count the stickers: the fewest stickers wins.
Share: which bug was the sneakiest, and what told you where it was?

subPlan: Do Now on paper, 3 minutes: find the mistake in 2 + 2 = 5, in Teh cat sat on the mat, and in a route card that says turn left when the flag is on the right.

Play Robo Route, chapter Debug Lab, in pairs for 20 minutes. Classes, then the lesson, then Play. If the game asks, the quest code is 6 1 1 0. Goal: 4 levels. No warm-up and no projector needed; playing signed out is fine.
Paper exit ticket: the half-sheet with three questions and the sentence frame. Collect it.

shortPeriod40.discuss: What was the bug on level 5, and how did you find it? Show step mode.
shortPeriod40.keep: the exit ticket is never cut

add: the Bug Cards twin (15 minutes) before Play
the fewest-edits stretch and level 7 after Play
Best Route, the next chapter, for 10 minutes (quest code 7 1 0 0 from the game's own menu): compare two routes and pick the better one

notes: Stars count edits: the fewest edits from the starter program earn three stars, so deleting everything is the slow and starless path.
The warm-up is a pre-test for unit 2: nobody is expected to know the answers yet. Say so before you start.
Debug mode works signed out, so the sub plan needs no login.
Shared devices: this is an even lesson, so partner B signs in; the gradebook and the Standards tab count the signed-in student.

steps.title: Today
steps.body:
Do Now: Find the mistake in each one: 2 + 2 = 5. Teh cat sat on the mat. A route card that says turn left when the flag is on the right.

Big idea: To fix a bug, step through the program, find where expected and actual first split apart, change that one thing, and test again.

We will talk about:
- What was the bug on level 5, and how did you find it?
- Why is deleting everything a slow way to fix a bug?

steps.title: Warm-up (live)
steps.body: Five quick questions. Your teacher shows them on the projector or starts them live. Nobody is expected to know them all yet.

steps.title: Play: Debug Lab
steps.body:
Goal: 4 levels. Stretch: finish the chapter, then 3 stars: the fewest edits on every level.
If the game asks for a quest code, it is 6 1 1 0.
Pairs: driver and navigator. Swap when the Swap! banner shows. The navigator reads the program out loud first and says Stop! in step mode.
Every level starts with a broken program. Press Step, find the first block that does something you did not expect, change only that block, and run it again.

steps.title: Exit ticket
steps.body: Three quick questions about bugs, testing and fixing.
